title: Tree of Coprimes
summary: Given a tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 , where each node has an associated value, determine for each node the closest ancestor whose value is coprime with the node's value.
statement: Given a tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 , where each node has an associated value, determine for each node the closest ancestor whose value is coprime with the node's value. If no such ancestor exists, return -1. The tree is defined by an integer array nums representing the values of the nodes and a 2D array edges representing the edges connecting the nodes. The root of the tree is node 0. Two values are coprime if their greatest common divisor (gcd) is 1. An ancestor of a node is any node on the shortest path from the node to the root, excluding the node itself.
constraints: Nodes form a tree rooted at zero and nums[i] is between 1 and 50.
For each node, return its nearest strict ancestor whose value is coprime with the node value, or -1.
hints: Only the latest active ancestor for each value 1..50 can be nearest.
DFS the rooted tree while maintaining a stack of (depth,node) for each value.
Before pushing the current node, scan coprime value stacks and choose the deepest top; pop after visiting children.
The active stacks exactly represent the root-to-parent path, and their tops dominate older equal-valued ancestors.
editorial: The active stacks exactly represent the root-to-parent path, and their tops dominate older equal-valued ancestors.

tests.explanation: Node one uses ancestor zero; node two also uses zero; node three uses nearest ancestor one, giving [-1,0,0,1].
Walking each root path and choosing the deepest coprime value gives [-1,0,-1,0,0,-1,-1].
